ledger.text: No skill or item reward is required.

items.text: "I found it the day we first made this place our home."
"It is exactly the right shape for keeping papers from blowing away."
"My oldest friend gave it to me."
"I was going to throw it away years ago, but then I got attached."
"It reminds me that small things can survive enormous storms."
places the replacement on a shelf

stone.name: The favorite stone
stone.text:
An elderly villager, (elder), has spent the morning searching for (elder.his/her) favorite stone. It is not a precious stone. It is not even particularly attractive. But (elder.he/she) has carried it for years.
(Adult) offers to help, while (child) asks what makes this particular stone so important. The elder replies, {A}

o1.text: The child finds the stone beneath a basket. The elder thanks (child.him/her) and tells the story of the day it was found.

o2.text: The adult finds three similar stones. The elder rejects them all with the solemn expertise of a jeweler inspecting diamonds.

o3.text: The stone turns out to have been in the elder's pocket all along. The elder says, "Excellent. The search was a success."

o4.text: Nobody finds the stone. The elder is disappointed, but the child offers a different one. The elder accepts it without pretending that it is the same.

o5.text: A father holding his infant recognizes the stone as the paperweight that has been sitting on the schoolhouse table. He returns it after the lesson ends.

o6.text: The elder quietly explains that the stone belonged to someone who is no longer alive. The child sits beside (elder.him/her) for a while.

sunset.text: By sunset, the village has moved on to other concerns. The elder {ENDING}.
